content: Closed shadow DOM (attachShadow({mode:'closed'})) blocks a PAGE script's direct host.shadowRoot access but is explicitly NOT a security boundary against a determined attacker manipulating ancestor/host-element CSS (opacity, position, z-index all apply from OUTSIDE the shadow tree) -- see DOM-based Extension Clickjacking research. A native browser-chrome popup window (browser.windows.create()) is architecturally immune to this entire attack class: it is a separate OS-level window, outside the page's DOM/CSSOM entirely, so no page-side opacity/z-index/focus() manipulation can touch it. The Popover API's top-layer rendering is a middle ground (browser-managed layer, resistant to z-index stacking) but is itself DOM-content and was shown exploitable via pointer-events:none overlay abuse in the same research.
